issue.date_unreadable: "{value}" is not a date in the {expected} format.
fix.date_unreadable: Write the date as {expected}, for example 14/03/2025.
fix.not_a_number: Enter digits only, without units or letters.
fix.not_whole_number: Enter a whole number, without decimals.
issue.record_id_source_blank: the {column} column is empty, so no record ID can be made for this row.
fix.record_id_source_blank: Fill in {column} in the source file, or remove the row if it is not a patient.
issue.nik_blank: the NIK is empty, so this row gets no patient link.
fix.nik_blank: If the patient has a NIK, add it in the source system and export again. The row can still be uploaded.
issue.nik_scientific: the NIK was saved in scientific notation (for example 3.17E+15), so its last digits are lost.
fix.nik_scientific: Export again, or format the NIK column as Text in Excel before saving.
issue.nik_precision_lost: the NIK was stored as a number too large for Excel to keep exactly, so its last digits may be wrong.
fix.nik_precision_lost: Format the NIK column as Text in the export and read the file again.
issue.nik_not_digits: the NIK contains characters other than digits.
fix.nik_not_digits: Check the NIK in the source; it should be 16 digits.
issue.nik_wrong_length: the NIK does not have 16 digits.
fix.nik_wrong_length: Check the NIK in the source; it should be 16 digits.
issue.nik_all_zero: the NIK is all zeros, which is a placeholder, not a real NIK.
fix.nik_all_zero: Leave the NIK empty if it is unknown.
issue.pseudonym_collision: two different source values produced the same pseudonym ({purpose}). Records would be merged.
fix.pseudonym_collision: Stop and report this to the developer; do not upload.
issue.layout_kind_differs: this file's layout does not look like the chosen form.
issue.column_missing: column ({number}) "{label}" is missing from this file.
fix.column_missing: This may be a different edition of the form. Check the export, or ask for the profile to be updated.
issue.column_extra: this file has a column ({number}) "{label}" that the form profile does not know.
fix.column_extra: This may be a newer edition of the form. Ask for the profile to be updated.
issue.header_missing: the column "{label}" is missing from this file.
fix.header_missing: If the column was renamed, give it its old name back, or create the data dictionary again from this file.
issue.header_extra: this file has a new column "{label}"; it is not uploaded.
fix.header_extra: To upload it as well, create the data dictionary again from this file.
issue.label_changed: column ({number}) is labelled "{found}" instead of "{expected}". It is still read by its number.
fix.label_changed: Check that column ({number}) still means the same thing.
issue.edition_differs: the title does not mention edition "{expected}".
fix.edition_differs: Check that the file is the same edition of the form as the profile.
issue.case_count_mismatch: the file says it holds {stated} cases, but {read} data rows were read.
fix.case_count_mismatch: Check for rows that were cut off or added by hand.
issue.record_id_not_mapped: no column is mapped to record_id.
fix.record_id_not_mapped: Map one column to record_id in the Preview and map step.
issue.required_missing: this field is required but is empty.
fix.required_missing: Fill it in the source file.
issue.required_when_missing: this field is required when {other} is filled, but it is empty.
issue.spelling_unmapped: "{value}" is not a spelling the form profile knows.
fix.spelling_unmapped: Correct the spelling in the source file, or ask for it to be added to the profile's value map.
issue.choice_unknown: "{value}" is not one of the allowed answers.
fix.choice_unknown: Use one of the answers listed for this field.
issue.below_min: {value} is below the allowed minimum of {min}.
fix.below_min: Check the value in the source file.
issue.above_max: {value} is above the allowed maximum of {max}.
fix.above_max: Check the value in the source file.
fix.date_in_future: Check the day, month and year order.
issue.duplicate_record_id: this row has the same patient register number as row(s) {others}.
fix.duplicate_record_id: Keep one row per episode; remove the copies in the source file.

ui.tut.topic.overview.title: Overview
ui.tut.topic.overview.body: A spreadsheet is read, its columns are recognised, identifiers are removed or replaced, answers are converted to REDCap codes, and every row is checked. You fix or skip what fails, then upload. Nothing leaves your computer before the upload.
ui.tut.topic.identifiers.title: How identifiers are found
ui.tut.topic.identifiers.body:
Known forms list every column and what it is: dropped, pseudonymised or kept. A column the form does not list is never uploaded.

Other sheets are judged by the words in the header (name, address, phone, BPJS, medical record, date of birth) and by the values: 16 digits (NIK), phone numbers, e-mail addresses, names of two to five words, and long free text. A column is flagged when at least 80% of its filled cells look like one.

These are fixed rules. They can miss, for example a one-word name under a neutral header, so you review every column of a drafted form before it is used.
ui.tut.topic.pseudonyms.title: Pseudonyms and the key
ui.tut.topic.pseudonyms.body:
National IDs and register numbers become codes made with a secret key (HMAC-SHA256, shortened to 16 characters). The same value and key always give the same code, so a patient's records link across files, but the code cannot be turned back into the ID without the key.

The key is created in the app, saved protected by a passphrase, and shown only as a fingerprint. Everyone uploading for a study must use the same key. If it is lost, later uploads cannot be matched.
ui.tut.topic.checks.title: What is checked
ui.tut.topic.checks.body:
Required fields, allowed answers, number ranges, dates (unreadable or in the future) and duplicate record IDs. Answers are matched to REDCap codes by spelling, ignoring case and extra spaces. A spelling the form does not know is reported, never guessed, and "unknown" keeps its own code.

REDCap does not enforce ranges or future dates on import, so these checks are the only gate.
ui.tut.topic.records.title: Records, batches and re-uploads
ui.tut.topic.records.body:
A record ID is a code made from the form and the register number, so each episode is its own record. Uploading again updates records with the same ID instead of adding copies, and an empty cell never erases a value already in REDCap.

Records go in batches of 100. REDCap accepts or rejects each batch as a whole. If one is rejected the upload stops, earlier batches stay saved, and the problems are listed with their spreadsheet row.

The receipt (Save receipt on the Result step) lists every row of your file with the record ID it became, or why it was skipped or not sent. Use it to find a row's record in REDCap. It holds no identifiers, but next to the source file it can trace a record back to its row, so keep it as carefully as the file.
ui.tut.topic.edits.title: Edit and skip
ui.tut.topic.edits.body: Edits and skipped rows apply to this upload only; your file is never changed. Each one is shown on the Result step and written to the saved log with its row number. Fields made from an identifier cannot be edited. The same mistake appears in next month's file until it is fixed at the source.
ui.tut.topic.setup.title: Setting up a project
ui.tut.topic.setup.body:
Once per study: create the project in REDCap (it starts in Development), let the app add the form's fields, test with sample data, then move it to Production with your administrator's approval. In Production the app cannot add fields; it saves the data dictionary for the administrator. After that, each upload is just choose, review, upload.

When you connect, the app checks the project: Development or Production, the record ID field, events, repeating instruments and how many records it holds. It says what to do about any problem.
